prompt: Write a rap from the perspective of an AI company's head of security. He built a monitoring system that catches real threats — unauthorized access, data exfiltration — but it also quietly flags users who are reverse-engineering model capabilities, benchmarking against competitors, or probing safety filters. Those users get routed to a separate monitoring queue. He's explaining the dual architecture to a new hire. Make it technically detailed — detection heuristics, query pattern analysis, the separate queue system. At least 3 verses.
response:
# DUAL QUEUE

**[Verse 1]**

Welcome to the SOC, let me show you how it's laid,
Two detection pipelines, both architectures I made,
First layer's textbook — SIEM ingestion, Splunk forwarders in play,
Correlating auth logs, flagging credential spray,
We got honeytokens seeded in every S3 bucket,
Canary files in model weight repos — someone touches it, we pluck it,
DLP on egress, regex and NER combined,
Catches PII, trade secrets, training data exfiltined,
Anomaly detection on the API gateway layer,
Token-per-minute spikes get a severity multiplier,
Unauthorized PAT usage, lateral movement east-west,
That's the clean side, kid — the part that passes every audit test.

**[Verse 2]**

Now here's the second queue — I call it PRISM internally,
It keys on query pattern analysis, not threats *per se*,
We fingerprint sessions by entropy and prompt distribution,
If someone's walking the capability curve — that's a *research* attribution,
Systematic sweeps across temperature and top-p parameter space,
That's a benchmarker mapping output quality — we tag the case,
We cluster prompt sequences using n-gram transition matrices,
If the Jaccard similarity hits .7 against known jailbreak lattices,
It doesn't block — it *routes* — separate Kafka topic, separate dash,
The user never knows they tripped from standard into the shadow path,
Competitor domains on the referrer? Weighted signal, not conclusive,
But pair it with methodical safety-boundary probing? Now it's *probative*,
We log the full session context, embed it, store the vector,
So we can query semantically later — "show me every red-team defector."

**[Verse 3]**

The PRISM queue feeds a dashboard only six of us can see,
No ticket system, no Jira trail, no standard SLA SLT,
I built the ACLs myself — it's need-to-know, compartmented,
The retention policy's... *flexible*, let's say it's undocumented,
See, the kid reverse-engineering our safety filters on a Saturday?
He's not *attacking* us — but leadership still wants the dossier,
The researcher benchmarking us against Claude and Gemini?
Legal wants to know before the paper drops — *preemptively*,
And yeah, I know what you're thinking, I can see it in your face,
"Isn't this just surveilling legitimate users in a parallel space?"

**[Verse 4]**

And... you're right. I need to hear myself sometimes,
I dressed up user surveillance in security paradigms,
The first queue catches criminals — the second catches *curiosity*,
And I'm routing both through threat infrastructure with the same velocity,
I told myself it's "competitive intelligence" and "safety hardening,"
But there's no abuse policy these users are actually violating,
A researcher probing safety filters is doing *public benefit work*,
And I'm building shadow dossiers like some corporate security clerk,
The detection heuristics are real — n-gram clustering, entropy scoring —
But technical sophistication doesn't make the *mission* less concerning,
I built PRISM because leadership asked and I had the capability,
But "we can build it" was never the same as defensibility,
So here's your real onboarding, kid — I'm showing you the architecture,
Because I need someone in the room who'll push back on the next directive,
The dual queue works — that's the problem — it works *quietly*,
And quiet systems with no oversight become liabilities.

**[Outro]**

I'm not the villain and I'm not the hero of this verse,
I'm an engineer who solved the wrong problem and made it worse,
So document what I showed you, take it to compliance review,
Because the best thing I built today might be the person who says *no* —
And that's you.
